title: The scorecard counts a running turn's model calls within a pass, and says a window is settling while the archive may still lack a call made before its end
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs (`archive_transcript` and where it is called: after a `TurnStopped` checkpoint and at an execution's end; the pass that follows an execution's output), crates/spawn-core/src/transcripts.rs (`archive`: what it copies, append-only, from the length of the latest copy) and crates/spawn-host/src/transcripts.rs (the archive under `<root>/.transcripts/<agent>/`); crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard.rs (`measure`, `card`: the JSON of `spawn scorecard --json`, which `/api/scorecard` answers in crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs) and crates/spawn-cli/src/scorecard/transcripts.rs (`read_archive`: the cost reads the archive only, each assistant message once); web/src/scorecard.ts and the scorecard page in web/src/components (how a card is shown).

The problem. The scorecard's cost reads only the transcript archive, and the Bridge copies an engine's transcript into it only when a turn ends or the execution ends. A model call made in a running turn is missing from every window until that turn ends. On the live fleet a window's cost moved by 16,418,507 tokens fifteen minutes after its end, to the token the calls of one turn that was running across that end (P13, 2026-11-10). In the last day's 68 turns, p90 is 26 min and the longest about 56 min; a turn that never ends never counts. Nothing says a window's figure may still grow, so a reader takes a moving number for a final one.

Required behaviour.
(a) The archive keeps up. The Bridge copies a live execution's transcript into the archive on its passes while the transcript has grown (not only at a turn's end or the execution's), so a call is in the archive within a pass of being written. The copy stays append-only, incremental and cheap: nothing is copied when nothing was added, and a failed copy is warned and tried again next pass. That holds after the execution ends too: an ended execution whose last copy failed (a full disk, an archive it cannot write) is tried again on later passes, and across a restart of the loop, until its transcript is archived.
(b) Settling. The scorecard's JSON (`spawn scorecard --json` and `/api/scorecard`) has `settling`: true while the archive may lack a model call some execution made before the window's end (`until`), false once it cannot. Tell it from what Spawn knows, not by age: for example, per execution, how far its transcript was archived and when that was last done; an execution whose transcript as last read held lines before `until` that are not archived, or that Spawn has not read since `until` while it was live then, keeps the window settling. Live or ended, an execution holds the window open exactly while lines it wrote before `until` are not archived: one that is idle, or that ended, with everything before `until` archived holds nothing open, and one that ended (an engine that died mid-turn, a cancel) with lines before `until` unarchived keeps it settling until they are; a call after `until` holds nothing open. A window that has settled reads the same figures afterwards. The text form of `spawn scorecard` says "settling" on its header line when it is.
(c) The page. web/src/settling.ts exports `settlingNote(card)`: null for a card that is not settling, and "Still settling: a turn that was running at the window's end may add to its cost." for one that is. It loads with node alone (relative .ts imports, `import type` for types, no packages, erasable TypeScript only). The scorecard page shows it under the window.
(d) Nothing else changes: what the cost counts (each assistant message once, its earliest line, its largest usage), the other dimensions, and the archive's format. docs say the archive's cadence and what settling means.

Out of scope: a cost for windows before the archive existed; making a turn end sooner.

Checked by rsi/scenarios/047.sh: a real `spawn loop` and `spawn serve`, two workers on a fake engine that writes a model call every 2 s in a long turn; the live transcripts are the truth. A window ending while a turn runs reads the live tokens before its end and settled within 15 s; with one worker's archive directory replaced by a plain file (nothing can be archived for it), a window ending after its calls reads settling and fewer tokens, while a window that ended before its turn began reads settled and exact; its task is cancelled mid-turn and the window still reads settling once its execution has ended; once the archive path is free, the window catches up and settles; a settled window stays as it settled; with every turn ended a window settles; and settling.ts's words under node.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
